forums: Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory
Magistrates Court of the Australian Capital Territory
note: Verified against legislation.act.gov.au on 2026-08-26. The Court Procedures Rules 2006 contain no time-reckoning rule of their own; the Legislation Act 2001 applies to every ACT Act and statutory instrument, so periods under the rules are worked out under s 151 (table item 2: a period 'after' a stated day or event excludes that day) and roll under s 151A to the next 'working day', which for a thing done at a court registry is a day the registry is open (dictionary, pt 1). Rule 6300(1) closes the registry on Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays, days between 26 December and 1 January, and days a registrar directs. The script approximates registry-open days with the weekend-and-public-holiday table; the 27-31 December closure is recorded as an uncertain window in that table so the script refuses rather than guesses, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the registry was open. Legislation Act s 152 (continuing effect of obligations) is not a time-reckoning rule and is not tabled. Magistrates Court civil claims are governed by the same rules (CPR r 6(1)); no Magistrates Court-specific period is tabled. An entry returned to pending-verification fails closed until re-verified.

computation_provisions.summary: Working out periods of time generally: applies to periods of 1 day or longer under an Act or statutory instrument (s 151(1)); by the table in s 151(2), a period described as beginning from or after a stated day, act or event does not include that day (item 2), a period described as ending at, by, on or with a stated day includes that day (item 3), and a period described as ending before a stated day excludes it (item 4).

computation_provisions.citation: Legislation Act 2001 (ACT) s 151A and dictionary, pt 1 (working day)
computation_provisions.summary: Periods of time ending on non-working days: if under an Act or statutory instrument something must or may be done on a particular day or within a particular period, and the day or the last day of the period is not a working day, it must or may be done on the next day that is a working day (s 151A(1)-(2)); the section is determinative for laws made or provisions inserted after 1 January 2006 (s 151A(3)-(4)), which includes the Court Procedures Rules 2006. 'Working day' means, for doing something at an office of a public entity, a day when the office is open, and otherwise a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday at the place where the thing must be done (dictionary, pt 1).

computation_provisions.summary: The registry must be open between 9.15 am and 1 pm and between 2 pm and 4.15 pm each day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday (r 6300(1)(a)), a day that falls between 26 December in a year and 1 January the following year (r 6300(1)(b)), or a day or part-day a registrar directs the registry to be closed (r 6300(1)(c)). Read with the 'working day' definition, these are the days on which a filing period cannot end.

period_rules.label: Notice of intention to respond, defence, or both, after service of originating claim
period_rules.trigger: Service of the originating claim on the defendant; the period runs after the day the claim is served
warnings: The filing date is the later of 28 days after service and, if the defendant makes an unsuccessful application under r 40 to set aside the originating process, 7 days after the day the application is refused (r 102(1)(b)); only the 28-day limb is computed.

Where an application for summary judgment under r 1146 is served before a defence is filed, the court may set the time for the defence (r 102(2)); proceedings started by originating application follow r 102(3) instead and are not computed here.

A defendant may take no step without a notice of intention to respond or defence except with leave (r 100); a defendant challenging jurisdiction or asserting an irregularity must file a conditional notice of intention to respond (r 111).

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed ACT public holiday; s 151A moves the last day to the next 'working day', which for filing means a day the registry is open (r 6300(1)) — the 27-31 December closure is an uncertain window in the holiday table and a registrar-directed closure is not, so confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP download of the official current republication PDF, text extracted with pdftotext; period and trigger in r 102(1)(a) confirmed exactly, r 102(1)(b)-(3), r 100 and r 111 read for the warnings.

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal and case summary to the Court of Appeal (no leave required)
period_rules.trigger: The day the order appealed from was made; the period runs after that day
warnings: This 28-day period applies 'in any other case' — where leave to appeal is not required. Where leave has been given, the notice of appeal and case summary must be filed within 7 days after the day leave is given or within the time the Court of Appeal sets (r 5405(1)(a)); leave to appeal from interlocutory orders is governed by div 5.4.2 and its own time rule (r 5312) — neither is computed here.

Further time may be allowed by the Supreme Court on an application filed before the end of the 28-day period (r 5405(1)(b)); after that, div 5.4.3 (leave to appeal out of time from final judgments) applies, and the Court of Appeal may at any time and for special reasons give leave to file (r 5405(2)).

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed ACT public holiday; s 151A moves the last day to the next 'working day', which for filing means a day the registry is open (r 6300(1)) — the 27-31 December closure is an uncertain window in the holiday table and a registrar-directed closure is not, so confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP download of the official current republication PDF, text extracted with pdftotext; period and trigger in r 5405(1)(b) confirmed exactly, r 5405(1)(a) and (2) read for the warnings.
